# task-e0c65be4: marker-centered 3×3 recoloring in solid fields

For this task, the input contains large uniform patches of color 3, embedded color-2 markers, and unrelated color-2 noise on color-0 background. For each color-2 cell that lies within one of the solid color-3 patches, recolor all color-3 cells in its 3×3 Moore neighborhood (center plus eight surrounding cells) to color 1. Keep the triggering 2 marker unchanged. Only change cells that were 3 in the original grid; preserve zeros, exterior 2s, and all other cells. Apply all marker stamps based on original markers, combining overlaps naturally.

## Evidence / distinctions

- Three supplied demo pairs establish that an embedded 2 makes a local 3×3 area of 1s, centered on that 2; the 2 remains 2.
- A stamp is clipped by the existing 3-patch: it does not paint over 0/background. E.g. in the 10×17 demo, the marker at row 3, col 4 is near the patch edge and only the in-patch cells change.
- Color-2 cells on the surrounding 0 background are unchanged. Do not process every 2 globally merely because it is near a patch; select markers located in the solid 3 areas.
- Adjacent marker triggers create unions of these 3×3 stencils; original 2s are preserved inside overlaps.

## Procedure

1. Identify the solid 3 regions and distinguish their embedded 2 markers from exterior 2 noise.
2. For each embedded marker, inspect the bounded 3×3 neighborhood.
3. Change original 3 cells in that neighborhood to 1; leave all other cells untouched.
4. Verify dimensions and every row. In the tested 16×27 case, the transformation preserved 16×27 dimensions and solved after one rejected first attempt.

## Prior failed hypothesis

An earlier attempted submission produced incorrect collateral changes because it mistakenly recolored original zeros and used faulty/inaccurate region selection.
